questions.question: Which of the following characteristics is TRUE for Aridisols?

options.a: They develop in humid tropical environments
options.b: They experience significant leaching due to high rainfall
options.c: They remain dry for most of the year and have slow soil formation
options.d: They contain high levels of organic matter accumulation

questions.explanation: Aridisols form in desert conditions, experience little to no leaching, and have low organic matter accumulation due to minimal vegetation.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of Entisols?

options.a: They are ancient soils with well-developed horizons
options.b: They are commonly found on highly weathered parent material
options.c: They lack well-developed horizons and are found on recent sediments
options.d: They have a significant accumulation of organic matter in the B horizon

questions.explanation: Entisols are young soils that lack well-defined horizons. They are commonly found on recently deposited materials like river sediments, beach sands, or volcanic ash.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following is a defining feature of Gelisols?

options.a: They are rich in iron and aluminum oxides
options.b: They are commonly found on highly weathered parent material
options.c: They are found in tropical climates with high temperatures
options.d: They are formed primarily in grasslands

questions.explanation: Gelisols are characterized by permafrost within 2 meters of the surface or gelic materials (frozen ground) within 1 meter, typically found in cold climates.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following best describes Oxisols?

options.a: They are fertile soils with high levels of silica
options.b: They are rich in iron, aluminum oxides, and kaolin, but low in silica
options.c: They are young soils found in temperate forests
options.d: They are soils with abundant trace nutrients due to minimal rainfall

questions.explanation: Oxisols are highly weathered soils found in tropical regions, rich in iron, aluminum oxides, and kaolin, but low in silica due to heavy rainfall and high temperatures.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following is a defining characteristic of Spodosols?

options.a: They are found in desert regions with minimal rainfall
options.b: They have an organic colloid layer complexed with iron and aluminum
options.c: They are highly fertile and support dense vegetation
options.d: They form in tropical rainforests with high temperature

questions.explanation: Spodosols are acidic soils with an organic colloid layer that is complexed with iron and aluminum, typically found in coniferous and deciduous forests in cooler climates.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following is a key characteristic of Alluvial Soils?

options.a: They have very high acidity and are mostly infertile
options.b: They are found in areas where the parent material is primarily volcanic ash
options.c: They are typically found in river valleys, floodplains, and deltas
options.d: They are rich in iron and aluminum oxides

questions.explanation: Alluvial soils are deposited by rivers and are typically found in river valleys, floodplains, and deltas, where the water flow carries fine sediments that enrich the soil.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Alluvial soils are generally considered to be fertile because of

options.a: They are high in organic matter
options.b: They are rich in essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium
options.c: They have a thick layer of clay that traps nutrients
options.d: They are always acidic and low in nutrients

questions.explanation: Alluvial soils are typically fertile because they are enriched with essential nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, which are deposited by the river water during flooding.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of Alluvial Soil?

options.c: Laterite

questions.explanation: Khadar and Bhangar are the two main types of alluvial soil found in river floodplains. Laterite is a different type of soil that forms in tropical climates with heavy rainfall and is rich in iron oxides.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Why are Alluvial Soils particularly important for agriculture?

options.b: They are resistant to erosion and support only sparse vegetation
options.c: They form in regions with minimal rainfall and high temperatures
options.d: They have high levels of salinity that support salt-tolerant crops

questions.explanation: Alluvial soils have a loose texture, are well-drained, and are rich in essential nutrients, which make them ideal for agriculture. They are easy to work with and support a wide variety of crops.[cite: 10]

questions.question: What is a major environmental concern regarding Alluvial Soils in river floodplains?

options.a: Soil erosion caused by water runoff and flooding
options.b: Accumulation of excess salt due to irrigation
options.c: Soil compaction from heavy machinery
options.e: Soil acidification due to volcanic ash deposition

questions.explanation: Soil erosion is a significant concern in alluvial soils found in floodplains. These soils can be washed away by heavy flooding or water runoff, leading to a loss of fertile topsoil.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which one of the following is a primary mineral?

options.c: Gypsum

questions.explanation: Primary minerals are those minerals which are formed from the original rocks and crystalline at high temperature Examples- quartz, feldspar, orthoclase, albite, micas, biotite, hornblende, and olivine.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which one of the following is a secondary mineral?

options.c: Montmorillonite

questions.explanation: Secondary Minerals- secondary minerals are formed by soluble substances from primary minerals and are precipitated and recrystallized. Examples- goethite, hematite, gibbsite, kaolinite, montmorillonite, chlorite, calcite and gypsum[cite: 10]

questions.question: ___ is defined as the process of disintegration and decomposition of rocks and minerals.

options.c: Stream erosion

questions.explanation: Weathering is defined as the process of disintegration and decomposition of rocks and minerals. Weathering is an integrated process of physical, chemical and biological processes[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following is/ are the most important agent of physical weathering?

options.c: Temperature and Moisture

questions.explanation: Temperature and Moisture. It is the first stage in the transformation of the parent materials into soil. Agents of physical weathering- temperature and water[cite: 10]

questions.question: Identify which of the following is/are the process of chemical weathering?

options.c: Reduction

questions.explanation: It mainly occurs due to solubility of minerals and formation of new substances takes place in chemical weathering. Chemical weathering takes place mainly by 6 process - solution, hydrolysis, hydration, oxidation, reduction, and carbonation.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Feldspar, amphiboles and mica are generally weathered by ___ process.

options.c: Carbonation

questions.explanation: Hydration- Inclusion of the water in a mineral structure, cause it to swell and leaving it more stressed and easily decomposed. Hydration reduce bonding and hardness of minerals which makes them susceptible to weathering. Ex-Feldspar, amphiboles and mica are weathered by hydration.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following chemical weathering processes occurs when oxygen reacts with minerals in rocks?

options.c: Oxidation

questions.explanation: Oxidation occurs when oxygen reacts with minerals, especially those containing iron, forming oxides like rust.[cite: 10]

questions.question: The process of leaching in chemical weathering involves

options.b: Dissolution and removal of soluble minerals by water
options.c: Breaking of rocks due to pressure release
options.d: Crystallization of salts in rock cracks

questions.explanation: Leaching occurs when water dissolves minerals and carries them away, altering soil composition.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Hydrolysis is an important chemical weathering process where minerals react with

options.c: Sulfuric acid

questions.explanation: In hydrolysis, water reacts with minerals, breaking them down into clay minerals and soluble ions.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following is a major agent of chemical weathering that forms carbonic acid when dissolved in water?

options.c: Sulphur dioxide

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide dissolves in water to form carbonic acid, which reacts with minerals like limestone, leading to their dissolution.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the B-horizon in a well-developed soil profile?

options.a: It is rich in organic matter and humus
options.b: It is composed mainly of unweathered parent material
options.c: It accumulates minerals leached from the upper layers (illuviation)

questions.explanation: The B-horizon, also known as the subsoil, is the zone where minerals such as iron, aluminum, and clay accumulate from the upper layers due to leaching (illuviation).[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following factors is most responsible for the development of distinct soil horizons over time?

options.c: Vertical movement of water and dissolved substances

questions.explanation: The primary driver of soil horizon formation is eluviation and illuviation, where water moves materials like clay, iron, and organic compounds downward, creating distinct layers.[cite: 10]

questions.question: In an extremely weathered tropical soil, the Oxisol, which horizon is typically absent or poorly developed?

options.c: B-horizon

questions.explanation: Oxisols form in warm, humid climates where intense leaching removes soluble materials, leaving behind a deep, highly weathered profile with weak or absent E-horizons.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which horizon is commonly referred to as the zone of eluviation, where leaching is most intense?

options.c: C-horizon

questions.explanation: The E-horizon (Eluvial Horizon) is characterized by loss of silicate clays, iron, and aluminum oxides, leaving behind a pale, leached layer.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the C-horizon is FALSE?

options.a: It consists of partially weathered parent material
options.b: It is located beneath the B-horizon in the soil profile
options.c: It contains significant amounts of organic matter and humus
options.d: It can eventually transform into soil through further weathering

questions.explanation: The C-horizon consists mostly of weathered rock and lacks significant organic content. Unlike the A or O horizons, it does not contain much humus.[cite: 10]

questions.question: In which type of climate would you expect to find the most well-developed soil profile with clearly distinct horizons?

options.c: Tropical rainforest with high temperature and rainfall

questions.explanation: Warm and wet climates accelerate chemical weathering and soil formation, leading to deep, well-developed profiles with distinct horizons, like in Oxisols.[cite: 10]

questions.question: What is the primary reason for the presence of a thick O-horizon in forested soils?

options.b: High accumulation of plant litter and organic matter
options.c: Slow movement of groundwater through soil

questions.explanation: Forested soils have a thick O-horizon due to continuous leaf litter and decomposition, enriching the soil with organic matter.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which horizon in a soil profile is most important for supporting plant life due to its high nutrient content?

options.c: E-horizon

questions.explanation: The A-horizon (topsoil) is rich in organic material and minerals, making it the most fertile and essential for plant growth.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics is NOT true for Alfisols?

options.a: They contain accumulations of aluminum and iron
options.b: They have horizons with significant clay accumulation
options.c: They require warm and moist conditions for at least three months of plant growth
options.d: They are the most abundant soil order worldwide
options.e: They constitute approximately 10.1% of global soils

questions.explanation: While Alfisols are an important soil order, they are not the most abundant globally. Entisols cover the largest area worldwide.[cite: 10]

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Andisols is FALSE?

options.a: They are derived from volcanic ash
options.c: They are highly fertile due to volcanic minerals
options.d: They cover approximately 10% of the world's ice-free land surface

questions.explanation: Andisols actually cover only about 1% of the world's ice-free land surface, not 10%.[cite: 10]
